identity.name: TELGE PROJECTS LIMITED
identity.industry: Global AEC Engineering Services & Digital BIM

summary.oneLiner: Telge Projects delivered a transformational FY26 with 57% revenue growth driven by the March acquisition of Edward Farr Architects and organic scaling, guiding for 60-70% CAGR while targeting sustained Q4-level margins (35% EBITDA) through higher billing rates ($45-60/hr) and AI integration. The strategic shift from pure detailing to full-lifecycle AEC services significantly expands addressable market and ticket sizes.

one-line thesis: Telge Projects delivered a transformational FY26 with 57% revenue growth driven by the March acquisition of Edward Farr Architects and organic scaling, guiding for 60-70% CAGR while targeting sustained Q4-level margins (35% EBITDA) through higher billing rates ($45-60/hr) and AI integration. The strategic shift from pure detailing to full-lifecycle AEC services significantly expands addressable market and ticket sizes.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs. 40.2cr (+57% YoY); EBITDA: Rs. 9.55cr (24% margin, up from ~20% prior year implied); PAT: Rs. 5.9cr (15% margin); Q4 Revenue: Rs. 14.4cr (+13.7% YoY, +58% QoQ); Q4 EBITDA Margin: 35%; Order Book: Rs. 25cr (visible); One-offs: Edward Farr acquisition contributed only ~1 month (Rs. 1.5cr revenue, Rs. 0.4cr PAT) to FY26 consolidated numbers; Employee cost ratio rose to 45% due to strategic leadership hiring ahead of growth.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 60-70% CAGR for FY27/FY28; Margins: Targeting Q4 levels sustained (35% EBITDA, 20-23% PAT); Order Inflow: Adding Rs. 4-5cr monthly; Capex/Commissioning: Organic capacity expansion in Nashik/Latur; no major debt-funded capex planned.
order book & pipeline: Rs. 25cr total active order book (Rs. 10cr from new architectural segment/Edward Farr); 80% sourced from US region; Pipeline: Rs. 6cr in bidding/RFQ stage with 2-4 week conversion window.
segment / subsidiary detail: Structural/Steel Detailing remains core but expanding into Architectural/Interior design post-Edward Farr acquisition; US subsidiaries handle business development/client relations while India centers (Nashik, Latur, Pune) handle execution; Ticket sizes increasing from Rs. 2-3cr to Rs. 8-10cr projects.
growth verticals / optionality: Cross-selling architectural services to existing structural clients and vice versa; Geographic expansion into Canada, New Zealand, Southeast Asia; Potential MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) acquisitions to complete full-service AEC offering; AI automation to scale output without linear headcount growth.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA margin at 35% driven by higher billing rates ($45-60/hr vs previous $25-35); Employee cost as % of revenue rose to 45% in FY26 due to upfront hiring of leadership/bench strength; Management expects employee cost ratio to stabilize as revenue scales without further leadership hires.
capex / expansion: Organic infrastructure investment in Nashik office (now operational) and Latur expansion; IPO proceeds partially allocated (Rs. 5cr provision) for future acquisitions rather than heavy fixed asset capex; Technology spend on AI tools (Claude, customized Tekla/Revit integrations).
capital allocation: IPO proceeds utilized for growth capital and acquisition provisions; No debt planned for next 2 years; Equity dilution/rights issue not anticipated in near term; M&A strategy focused on tuck-in acquisitions (like Edward Farr) at ~2.5x EBITDA multiples.
risks & watch-items: Receivable days expanded to 108 days (mostly related party, being cleared); Dependence on US market (80% of order book); Potential commoditization of low-end modeling via AI; Execution risk in integrating multiple US acquisitions; Seasonality (Q2 typically slower).
management quality / tone: Highly confident and ambitious; Emphasis on 'transformational' year and global scalability; Transparent about upfront cost investments for future gains; Aggressive on growth guidance (60-70% CAGR) but conservative on debt.
non-obvious takeaways: Subsidiaries have zero attrition vs 10% in India; 60-70% of revenue is recurring from existing clients despite project-based nature; Management considers acquired subsidiaries' growth as 'organic' going forward since execution is fully integrated in India; Q4 strength driven by US decision-making cycles.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for cost-effective, high-quality engineering design amid US labor shortages | Telge Projects Limited | beneficiary | High | Unique hybrid model (US sales/India execution) allows 35%+ margins while competitors struggle with local labor costs; AI integration further widens moat. |
